newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia manufacturing output seen improving.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia manufacturing output seen improving.

text.p: Malaysia's manufacturing production is likely to improve in the last quarter of 1996 in line with an expected increase in domestic and export sales, the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research (MIER) said.
In its quarterly Business Conditions survey, the government-backed think-tank said that of 168 companies surveyed, 51 percent expected output to increase and eight percent predicted a decline.
Significant increases in production are expected from manufacturers of plastics, rubber, chemical and paper products, MIER said.
Thirty-eight percent of those surveyed projected an improvement in domestic sales and 34 percent forecast a rise in exports in the fourth quarter.
Manufacturers of rubber goods, food, paper and chemical products were optimistic about local sales in the fourth quarter.
Exporters of metal, electrical and machinery goods also expected a better performance, MIER said.
"Buoyant performance in these sectors should help to mitigate an expected downturn in sales of food, wood-based and chemical products abroad," it said.
The majority of firms in all sectors anticipated prices, wage costs and employment to remain fairly stable, the think-tank said.
Seventy-four percent of the firms surveyed expected no change in the price of their goods, while 65 percent and 67 percent expected wage cost per unit and employment to remain constant.
The survey said while a majority of the firms recorded no change in sales volume, 27 percent reported increases in the third quarter compared with 29 percent in the previous quarter.

A downturn in sales of electrical products, which began this year, continued to prevail, with 44 percent of manufacturers reporting a drop in the third quarter compared with 29 percent in the previous quarter.
Thirty-six percent of the firms reported an increase in production in the third quarter compared with 33 percent in the second quarter.
The survey said in the third quarter, 67 percent of the firms reported no change in investment levels, while 25 percent recorded an increase and seven percent recorded a fall.
